title: Naturality of the explicit unit factor-order comparison
statement: For a quasi-compact separated scheme map f:X→S, a quasi-coherent E on S, and affine linear equivalences e natural for coherentEdgePullback and coherentEdgeRho [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-base-change-edge-naturality], the family obtained by composing e with the explicit structural-unit symmetry [new-unit-affine-symmetry] is natural for affineRealizationRestriction and etaleTensorSectionsRestriction [def-weil-pbc-affine-cohomology-comparison-data]. This fixes the family explicitly and asserts just the restriction square, not its existence or scalar compatibility.

proof.text: Identify the section-normalized adjunction with the chosen adjunction by uniqueness. The conjugate-unit identity identifies their composition maps and shows structural-unit normalization respects composition. Source and target naturality of module cohomology normalize both restriction maps. The two pullback projections show symmetry commutes with base change, so cohomology functoriality gives the restriction square. Apply the given naturality of e and identify the section restriction using the same composition identity. Identify the affine restriction through the constructed generic tensor-composite cohomology restriction, whose coefficient transport has a named equality proof. This retains the same adjunct while fixing its scheme and category interfaces before specialization. Use section evaluation with exactly the chart group endpoints, normalize identity-functor presentations of chart schemes, and evaluate the three section maps in their specified order. Use private pointwise function views of symmetry and coefficient cohomology maps to fix their underlying types. Unpack the étale chart and arrow records, give the underlying arrows their scheme types, and eliminate the arrow equality before composing the pointwise equations. The comparison-family evaluation and tensor-section evaluation then give the original square. Give the supplied linear-equivalence family a private constructed function view and prove its naturality directly from e_natural before specializing the pointwise square to charts. This keeps linear-equivalence coercions out of the final kernel conversions.
